items.title: Boundary versus ownership
items.scenario: A municipal flood-warning project defines its system-of-interest as the authority's own warning service, excluding supplier infrastructure. A commercial rainfall feed is required, and the authority remains accountable for warnings when that feed is delayed.
items.question: How should the supplier be represented?

choices.A: Allocate availability to the supplier contract and verify internal warning logic with timely inputs, assessing each organization separately.
choices.B: Include supplier infrastructure inside the implementation boundary and allocate its availability controls to the authority responsible for warnings.
choices.C: Model supplier delay as a fixed external parameter so internal design can proceed before delayed-feed response ownership is agreed.
choices.D: Keep the supplier external to the chosen boundary; specify its dependency contract and the authority's response to delayed data.

items.title: Conflicting outcomes
items.scenario: Airport operations wants shorter gate turnaround; maintenance wants enough inspection time; crews report increasing last-minute changes. The team proposes automation of the inspection signoff. No causal study is available.
items.question: Which proposed actions establish a defensible decision basis from the supplied facts, without first assuming a cause or a target?

choices.A: Define the competing turnaround, inspection and change-control outcomes, including the operating conditions in which each must be protected.
choices.B: Use maintenance ownership of signoff to assign it primary responsibility for delay, then measure the effect of automating its approval step.
choices.C: Adopt the fastest observed turnaround as the acceptance threshold for the new process, then investigate exceptions when that threshold is missed.
choices.D: Trace the timing of late changes, inspection work and decisions across roles to distinguish their contributions to the observed turnaround.

items.title: End of service
items.scenario: A sensor network stores configuration keys in modules expected to remain installed for fifteen years. The design review covers commissioning and operation but not replacement or retirement.
items.question: Which actions are justified by the supplied lifecycle facts without adding an unprovided policy or disposal requirement?

choices.A: Adopt physical destruction of every retired module as the required disposal method, based on the stated presence of configuration keys.
choices.B: Define who will provide compatible replacements and spares if the supplier ends support during the planned fifteen-year service period.
choices.C: Define how replacement modules receive and verify the authorized configuration before they are returned to the operating sensor network.
choices.D: Define credential retirement and data-removal outcomes for removed modules, then select disposal methods against the applicable requirements and evidence.

items.title: Reliability across a mission
items.scenario: Two alternatives have the same measured failure frequency during operation. One restores within minutes after a fault; the other requires a specialist visit. Missions are daily and unattended sites have limited access.
items.question: What conclusion follows?

choices.A: Compare failures over equal exposure and use the tighter uncertainty interval to choose between alternatives with similar observed reliability.
choices.B: Select the faster-restoring alternative and resolve purchase cost and specialist access during deployment planning.
choices.C: Compare restoration and access conditions alongside failure occurrence before estimating mission availability and lifecycle effort.
choices.D: Require field observations of both restoration processes before developing an availability estimate suitable for the purchase decision.

items.title: A shared event in a tree
items.scenario: A fault tree is (A AND B) OR (A AND C). Event A represents the same loss of a shared supply wherever it appears.
items.question: Which minimal cut sets follow from that Boolean model?

choices.A: The minimal cut sets are {A,B} and {A,C}; either conjunction is sufficient, and both occurrences of A represent the same event.
choices.B: The minimal cut sets are {A1,B} and {A2,C}; repeated positions represent separate instances when evaluating the tree.
choices.C: The minimal cut sets are {A} and {B,C}; factoring the shared term separates its failure from the downstream conjunction.
choices.D: The minimal cut set is {A,B,C}; both branches appear beneath one top event and contribute to its combined condition.

items.title: A warning that causes more work
items.scenario: An alarm threshold is lowered. Detection rises, but operators receive many more alarms and begin delaying acknowledgment. Reported unresolved incidents also rise.
items.question: Which next model is most useful?

choices.A: Model how alarm load changes attention, acknowledgment and escalation, then connect those responses to unresolved events.
choices.B: Identify operators and shifts with the longest acknowledgment delays, prioritizing refresher training before changing detector or escalation settings.
choices.C: Refit the detector threshold against incident labels, increasing the penalty for missed events to offset the rise in unresolved cases.
choices.D: Apply the earlier acknowledgment distribution to the new alarm rate to estimate the additional staffing required.

items.title: Zero observed failures
items.scenario: An engineer tests twenty identical units for one hour each and observes no failures. The report claims the system failure probability is zero.
items.question: Which response is most appropriate?

choices.A: Report twenty unit-hours with zero events; any reliability estimate needs an explicit exposure model, assumptions and uncertainty.
choices.B: Use reciprocal accumulated exposure as a conservative failure-rate estimate and carry that single rate into reliability planning.
choices.C: Exclude zero-event observations from reliability comparison and use the test to plan a campaign long enough to observe failures.
choices.D: Pool the twenty unit-hours into a survival duration and compare it directly with the uninterrupted mission required of one unit.

items.title: Coverage with an unrealistic assumption
items.scenario: A formal check proves that every accepted request is eventually served under an assumption that the shared resource is continuously available. Deployed operation allows outages and bounded recovery.
items.question: Which next step best strengthens the evidence?

choices.A: Add outage handling to the implementation while retaining the established liveness contract, then test the new recovery procedures.
choices.B: Review the availability assumption and analyze outage/recovery behavior, preserving the existing proof as conditional evidence.
choices.C: Repeat the check with more requests to establish that the result scales with demand.
choices.D: Retain the proof and verify resource availability separately, treating successful recovery tests as support for the original continuous-availability assumption.

items.title: Decomposition loses a condition
items.scenario: The parent requires emergency shutdown on loss of either pressure sensing or temperature sensing. Two children require a diagnostic on pressure loss and a diagnostic on temperature loss. The allocation matrix links both children to the parent.
items.question: What remains missing?

choices.A: Add measurable deadlines to each diagnostic so the two children fully specify the parent response to either sensing loss.
choices.B: The children require an allocation to separate sensors, because the parent's either-condition wording implies that sensing and shutdown must have redundant hardware paths.
choices.C: Both loss conditions are covered, but a common diagnostic identifier is needed to consolidate the children under the parent.
choices.D: The decomposition retains the two diagnostic triggers but omits the required shutdown response; define how either diagnosis causes the specified system action.

items.title: Resolving conflicting authorities
items.scenario: A signed contract requires a maximum mass of 40 kg. A later meeting note proposes 45 kg to improve endurance but contains no approval. The team is preparing a design trade.
items.question: Which treatment preserves the decision basis?

choices.A: Use the newer meeting value for preliminary trades while retaining 40 kg in the contract register, then reconcile the two at the next baseline review.
choices.B: Trade options across the 40–45 kg range and recommend the highest-scoring design, treating the meeting note as evidence that the sponsor accepts that range.
choices.C: Use 40 kg as the obligation and 45 kg as a proposed change, showing the design consequence and the approval needed to adopt it.
choices.D: Freeze the mass-dependent concept comparison until the change is approved, so exploratory results cannot influence a decision made against the still-binding contractual limit.

items.title: Mars Climate Orbiter: a contract existed
items.scenario: The 1999 Mars Climate Orbiter investigation reports that a ground software interface specified metric impulse data, while a producer supplied English-unit data. The report also identifies verification and communication weaknesses.
items.question: Which action best transfers this lesson to a new project?

choices.A: Require a common engineering unit in every software module, then use static type checks to demonstrate that integration and operational transition risks are addressed.
choices.B: Centralize quantity conversion in one integration component, then verify its calculations while retaining each producer's existing assumptions about units and message meaning.
choices.C: Add unit labels and approval signatures to the controlled interface specification, using that record as producer acceptance evidence.
choices.D: Verify actual producer-consumer exchanges against explicit unit semantics and representative operational data, with ownership for detecting and resolving discrepancies.

items.title: Ownership at an interface
items.scenario: A sensor supplier guarantees nominal one-second updates. The controller designer assumes the latest value is usable for five seconds. Neither defines timestamps, loss detection or clock alignment.
items.question: Which clarification has the highest immediate value?

choices.A: Confirm the supplier's average update performance over representative workloads, then retain the controller's five-second limit if it exceeds the observed mean interval.
choices.B: Agree which team reports missing updates, then retain independent local clock references because freshness is checked separately within each organization's component.
choices.C: Choose the protocol and retry policy, then derive allowable data age from the resulting maximum retry duration.
choices.D: Define timestamps, age limits, guaranteed update bounds and invalid-data responses so both parties can establish when a measurement is usable.

items.title: A reversible trial
items.scenario: Two scheduling policies meet hard constraints in preliminary analysis. A can be trialed at one site with rapid rollback; B requires a year-long infrastructure change. Demand forecasts are uncertain and likely to change within six months.
items.question: Which factor belongs in the decision?

choices.A: Include the cost and value of reversible learning: compare how each choice exposes the project to uncertain demand and later migration.
choices.B: Prefer the reversible trial and defer migration analysis until measured demand establishes whether another architecture is needed.
choices.C: Prefer B if its expected long-run performance is higher, then absorb forecast changes within its infrastructure commitment rather than reopening the architecture decision.
choices.D: Compare both options at the mean demand forecast and discount future operating costs, leaving trial reversibility outside the score to avoid double-counting uncertainty.

items.title: Build, buy and the supporting system
items.scenario: A defense logistics team can buy a sensor that meets laboratory accuracy requirements. Field repair, export/access constraints, supply continuity and integration with existing maintenance records remain unresolved.
items.question: What should a build/buy comparison include?

choices.A: Compare laboratory performance and purchase cost, allocating support and integration constraints to the selected option’s implementation plan.
choices.B: Compare delivered field capability, including sensing, integration, support and supply constraints; keep uncertain assumptions and their decision owners explicit.
choices.C: Compare estimated lifecycle costs using a common contingency factor, then select the cheaper option if the supplier can document compliance with the sensor specification.
choices.D: Compare the sensor functions that the program directly controls, then evaluate external integration and supply constraints separately so vendor limitations do not bias architecture selection.

items.title: An estimate becomes a fact
items.scenario: A preliminary model assumes a 20-minute restoration time because no maintenance data exists. Several slides later, the executive summary calls this the measured restoration time.
items.question: What correction is needed?

choices.A: Relabel the calculated outcomes as predictions while retaining the 20-minute input in the executive summary, because modeling distinguishes them from field observations.
choices.B: Restore the value's assumption status and identify which conclusions depend on it, preserving useful calculations as explicitly conditional results.
choices.C: Exclude the model's results from the decision package until restoration data is obtained, because an assumed input cannot support any useful engineering comparison.
choices.D: Substitute a longer restoration allowance and retain the conclusion, using conservatism to cover the missing measurements.

items.title: US Airways 1549: decision time in a simulation
items.scenario: The NTSB's report on the 2009 US Airways 1549 accident distinguishes immediate-return simulator attempts from scenarios including crew decision time. An immediate turn toward an airport does not represent the same starting conditions as the actual crew's situation.
items.question: What is the strongest transferable lesson?

choices.A: Compare each alternative’s best successful trajectory and use its performance margin to determine the preferred crew response.
choices.B: Compare alternatives using the information and recognition-to-action timing available at the actual decision point, stating what each simulation assumes.
choices.C: Compare aircraft capability from the instant of hazard onset, then treat recognition and diagnosis as separate training factors outside the alternative-feasibility assessment.
choices.D: Use the delayed simulator attempt as the representative case, then extrapolate its outcome to the range of feasible return decisions in the actual event.

items.title: Columbia: routine success and unresolved evidence
items.scenario: The 2003 Columbia Accident Investigation Board analyzes both physical damage mechanisms and organizational practices. A contemporary team argues that a recurring anomaly is acceptable because previous missions succeeded.
items.question: What should a review require?

choices.A: Estimate anomaly acceptability from the proportion of successful affected missions, then revisit the decision when another anomaly changes that rate.
choices.B: Explain the anomaly mechanism and evidence, including whether prior successes cover the present conditions and what remains unresolved.
choices.C: Ask the subsystem owner to confirm that the current event resembles previous cases, then carry forward the previously accepted disposition.
choices.D: Retain the disposition until anomaly frequency materially changes, while improving collection of flight performance data.

items.title: London 2012: a supplier cannot deliver
items.scenario: The National Audit Office's post-Games review describes extensive operational preparation for London 2012 and contingency action when the security contractor could not provide planned staffing.
items.question: Which preparation best transfers to a new major event?

choices.A: Increase staffing surveillance before the event and track recruitment milestones, using early forecasts as the main control on delivery risk.
choices.B: Contract with reserve suppliers and verify their commercial commitments, activating the reserve contract when the primary provider reports a shortfall.
choices.C: Rehearse plausible shortfalls with the decision authorities and reserve resources, verifying readiness and changes needed to sustain operations.
choices.D: Define an escalation organization and rehearse executive decisions, leaving reserve staff preparation to the agency assigned responsibility during activation.

items.title: Reporting disagreement
items.scenario: Two reviewers disagree about whether an old environmental test covers a revised connector. One cites unchanged materials; the other cites a changed seal geometry. A report must be delivered today.
items.question: Which report is most useful?

choices.A: Explain both evidence arguments, isolate whether seal geometry changes test applicability, and name the decision or investigation needed to resolve it.
choices.B: Keep the old test provisionally applicable because materials are unchanged, flagging geometry for confirmation in the next scheduled environmental campaign.
choices.C: Declare the old test inapplicable because geometry changed, remove its trace link, and recommend repeating the complete environmental qualification.
choices.D: Ask a third reviewer to resolve the disagreement by today, reporting the majority judgment with the original evidence attachments.

items.title: Choosing a useful view
items.scenario: A review board cannot tell who controls motion during startup, normal operation, manual stop and recovery. It already has a component hierarchy with complete part names.
items.question: Which additional view best answers the question?

choices.A: Add an interface view showing command and status connections, including each message direction and the component that sends it.
choices.B: Add a state and authority view linking transitions and guards to the components permitted to enable, stop or resume motion.
choices.C: Add a function-allocation view linking each motion-related function to its implementing component, including the organization responsible for each function.
choices.D: Add a nominal startup sequence showing operator commands and component responses, using its final operating state to represent motion authority.

items.title: TCP: acknowledgment at the right layer
items.scenario: RFC 793 (1981) explains that TCP acknowledgment means the receiving TCP has taken responsibility for data, not necessarily that it has been delivered to the end user. A system logs TCP acknowledgment as proof that a remote operator acted.
items.question: What should the review conclude?

choices.A: Add retries until the connection receives an acknowledgment within its timeout, then use the bounded exchange to establish completed action.
choices.B: Supplement TCP receipt with an application-server delivery log, treating successful delivery to the operator console as evidence of action.
choices.C: The log establishes transport receipt at that layer; operator action requires a relevant observation and acknowledgment in the application workflow.
choices.D: Have the operator console acknowledge message display and use that event to close the action, retaining transport logs for diagnosis.

items.title: DNS: a historical design trade
items.scenario: RFC 1034 (1987) describes distributed maintenance and caching, including a trade among acquisition cost, update speed and cache accuracy. A team proposes a very long cache lifetime to reduce server load for rapidly changing control data.
items.question: What transfers from the source?

choices.A: Remove caching from the control path and accept the extra server load, treating rapidly changing data as incompatible with local reuse.
choices.B: Choose a lifetime shorter than the mean update interval, then use that relationship to justify freshness independently of individual control actions.
choices.C: Set the lifetime from measured server-load savings and reduce it when operators report that stale values are affecting control decisions.
choices.D: Evaluate update behavior and stale-data consequences for this application; the source explains the trade but does not provide its acceptable limits.

items.title: A supplier changes its service contract
items.scenario: A cloud service previously guaranteed delivery of events in order. Its new version preserves all events but allows reordering. The consumer uses arrival order to authorize a sequence of physical actions.
items.question: Which review scope is necessary?

choices.A: Revalidate message schemas and event counts, then keep existing action tests if every transmitted event reaches the consumer without field changes.
choices.B: Add a reorder buffer with a fixed waiting period, then retain the consumer logic and tests once normal ordering is restored.
choices.C: Review ordering assumptions in consumer state and authority logic, including recovery, delay and duplicates, and reassess the affected verification evidence.
choices.D: Requalify the consumer’s physical-action components, treating the cloud change as a supplier concern once the event delivery count is verified.

items.title: A rejected alternative becomes relevant
items.scenario: A system chose a wired sensor because radio coverage was poor at remote sites. The new deployment is indoors with existing radio infrastructure, but battery replacement staffing is limited.
items.question: What should the concept review do?

choices.A: Reopen the alternatives against indoor coverage and limited battery support, retaining the old rationale while evaluating changed assumptions and lifecycle costs.
choices.B: Retain wired sensing for the first indoor release and reassess radio after measured maintenance costs justify reopening the earlier trade.
choices.C: Compare wired and radio using the original criteria and weights, updating coverage estimates to reflect the indoor infrastructure now available.
choices.D: Select radio provisionally because the original coverage concern is resolved, then assign battery staffing to the deployment support plan.
